question: What is the key trait of a polyvalent nurse?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on surgical nursing care
options.D: Working only in hospital management roles

explanation: Spot on! A polyvalent nurse is cross-trained in different fields, meaning they can comfortably move and work across various hospital departments. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why are polyvalent nurses a lifesaver during staff shortages?

options.A: They only work during night shifts
options.B: They do not require supervision from senior staff
options.C: They can be deployed easily to different hospital units
options.D: They demand lower salaries than specialized nurses

explanation: You got it! Because they have a mix of skills, hospitals can easily move them to busy or understaffed wards to keep patient care running smoothly. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h1)

question: In polyvalent nursing, what does giving 'holistic care' mean?

options.A: Focusing strictly on medication administration schedules
options.B: Prioritizing hospital administrative rules over patients
options.C: Treating only the specific disease diagnosed by a doctor
options.D: Looking at the whole person including body and mind

explanation: Exactly! Holistic care means looking at the patient as a complete human being—body, mind, and spirit—rather than just focusing on a single symptom. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: What keeps a polyvalent nurse eager to keep learning on the job?

options.A: The desire to become a hospital administrator eventually
options.B: The need to maintain skills across many different medical fields
options.C: Pressure from hospital managers to reduce operating costs
options.D: Strict government laws requiring annual license renewals

explanation: Well done! Since they work in diverse units, polyvalent nurses always stay on their toes, updating their knowledge across multiple specialties. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h2)

question: What does 'multi-skilling' mean for a nurse?

options.A: Managing hospital finances and staff rosters
options.B: Possessing certified competence in various clinical tasks
options.C: Being able to perform minor surgeries without a doctor
options.D: Knowing how to operate heavy hospital machinery only

explanation: Correct! Multi-skilling is all about mastering a variety of practical nursing procedures so you can handle different types of patient care. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h3)

question: A nurse smoothly moves from managing an IV drip in the ER to dressing a wound in the surgical ward. What is this nurse showing?

options.C: Inability to focus on one single duty

explanation: Spot on! Being able to switch tasks across different units proves you have great clinical versatility and multi-skilling abilities. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h3)

question: Where can polyvalent nurses put their skills to work?

options.C: Across various urban and rural health facilities
options.D: Exclusively in private intensive care units

explanation: You nailed it! Because they are so adaptable, polyvalent nurses can fit right into almost any healthcare setting, from city hospitals to village clinics. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why is adaptability so important for nurses working in rural clinics?

options.A: They follow rigid routines that never change
options.B: They often face limited resources and must adjust quickly
options.C: They deal exclusively with surgical trauma cases daily
options.D: They do not need to interact with other health workers

explanation: Correct! Rural clinics often lack heavy equipment and specialized staff, so nurses have to be resourceful and flexible to help their patients. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h4)

question: How does a polyvalent nurse usually support the healthcare team?

options.A: Deciding the hospital budget for medical supplies
options.B: Writing hospital policies without consulting staff
options.D: Acting as a communication link between different specialists

explanation: Spot on! They bridge the gaps between various medical professionals, keeping communication flowing for the patient's benefit. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h5)

question: Why is teamwork and good communication so great for patients?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any nursing documentation
options.B: It lowers the cost of private hospital rooms
options.C: It reduces the total time doctors spend in the hospital
options.D: It prevents errors and ensures coordinated treatment

explanation: You got it! When everyone on the healthcare team communicates well, patient care becomes much safer and better organized. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h5)

question: When does a polyvalent nurse need critical thinking the most?

options.A: When ordering food supplies for the hospital canteen
options.B: When organizing the staff holiday duty roster
options.C: When filing daily paperwork at the nurses' station
options.D: When analyzing sudden changes in a patient's condition

explanation: Exactly! Critical thinking helps you spot trouble early, figure out what's happening when a patient suddenly takes a turn for the worse, and act fast. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h6)

question: What should a polyvalent nurse do if standard supplies run out during an emergency?

options.A: Abandon the patient until fresh supplies arrive
options.B: Use problem-solving skills to find safe alternatives
options.C: Wait for the hospital director to fix the issue
options.D: Blame the junior nursing staff for the shortage

explanation: Well done! Resourcefulness is key in nursing. Finding safe alternatives keeps patients protected even when supplies are low. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h6)

question: What should you do if asked to perform a task outside your training and scope of practice?

options.A: Decline the task based on your scope of practice
options.B: Perform it anyway to help out the busy department
options.C: Pretend you completed the task on the patient's chart
options.D: Ask a patient to teach you how to do it

explanation: Spot on! Always stay within your legal and certified scope of practice. Patient safety comes first, and it's okay to say no to things you aren't trained for yet. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h7)

question: Which of these actions goes AGAINST a nurse's ethical duties?

options.A: Sharing patient medical details on social media
options.B: Advocating for the best interests of the sick person
options.C: Protecting patient privacy and medical confidentiality
options.D: Respecting the cultural beliefs of every patient

explanation: Correct! Patient confidentiality is sacred. Sharing patient details online is a serious breach of ethics and professional trust. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h7)

question: What major staffing headache in Nigerian healthcare do polyvalent nurses help solve?

options.A: A lack of patients seeking medical treatment
options.B: Shortages of specialized nursing personnel in facilities
options.C: An oversupply of doctors in rural health centers
options.D: Excessive funding for primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! They are a wonderful solution for bridging the gap where specialized nurses are hard to find. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h8)

question: A rural health clinic has only two nurses on duty. Which staffing approach ensures the best care for the community?

options.A: Firing the nurses and hiring administrative clerks
options.B: Employing polyvalent nurses trained in multiple care areas
options.C: Restricting care strictly to adult male patients
options.D: Closing the clinic until a specialist doctor arrives

explanation: Spot on! Having polyvalent nurses means a small team can safely and confidently handle a wide variety of health needs in the community. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T7#GNS112_U1_T7_h8)
